source_text: Οὗτος οὖν μόνος καὶ κατὰ πάντων θεὸς λόγον πρῶτον ἐννοηθεὶς ἀπογεννᾷ, οὐ λόγον ὡς φωνήν, ἀλλ᾿ ἐνδιάθετον τοῦ παντὸς λογισμόν. Τοῦτον μόνον ἐξ ὄντων ἐγέννα· τὸ γὰρ ὂν αὐτὸς ὁ πατὴρ ἦν, ἐξ οὗ τὸ γεννηθέν. Αἴτιον τοῖς γινομένοις λόγος ἦν, ἐν ἑαυτῷ φέρων τὸ θέλειν τοῦ γεγεννηκότος, οὐκ ἄπειρος τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς ἐννοίας· ἅμα γὰρ τῷ ἐκ τοῦ γεννήσαντος προελθεῖν, πρωτότοκος τούτου γενόμενος φωνή, ἔχει ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὰς ἐν τῷ πατρὶ προεννοηθείσας ἰδέας, ὅθεν κελεύοντος πατρὸς γίνεσθαι κόσμον τὸ κατὰ ἓν λόγος ἀπετελεῖτο ἀρέσκων θεῷ.
pass_a_gloss: This one therefore alone and according to all God, having been conceived, first begot the logos, not the logos as sound, but the inward thought of all reasoning. This one alone he generated from what exists; for the one who exists was the Father himself, from whom the generated one. The logos was the cause for the things that come into being, carrying in itself the will of the one who generated, not without the Father's conception; for at the same time as proceeding from the one who generated, having become the firstborn of this, sound, it has in itself the ideas preconceived in the Father, whence, the Father commanding to make the world, the logos according to the one was being completed, pleasing to God.

pass_b_english: This one, therefore, alone and as God over all, having been conceived, first begot the Logos—not the Logos as sound, but as the inward thought of all reasoning. He alone generated this one from what exists, for the One who exists was the Father himself, from whom the generated one came. The Logos was the cause for the things that come into being, carrying within himself the will of the one who generated him, not apart from the Father's conception; for at the same time as he proceeded from the one who generated him, having become the firstborn of this, sound, he holds within himself the ideas preconceived in the Father, whence, the Father commanding the world to be made, the Logos accomplished each thing in turn, pleasing to God.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both fail to correctly translate the phrase 'τὸ κατὰ ἓν λόγος ἀπετελεῖτο' (the logos according to the one was being completed/accomplished). Pass A translates it as 'the logos according to the one was being completed', which is a literal but semantically broken rendering of the Greek structure. Pass B translates it as 'the Logos accomplished each thing in turn', which is a significant interpretive leap/paraphrase that adds 'each thing in turn' to account for 'κατὰ ἓν' (one by one/according to the one), but it loses the specific grammatical relationship of the Logos being the subject of the completion in relation to the Father's command. More critically, Pass A's translation of 'καὶ κατὰ πάντων θεὸς' as 'and according to all God' is a failure of syntax; the Greek means 'and God over all' or 'God according to all [things]', but 'according to all God' is nonsensical in English and fails to preserve the agency/nature of God described.
reasons: Pass A: 'and according to all God' for 'καὶ κατὰ πάντων θεὸς' is a syntactic failure that obscures the meaning of God's relationship to all things.
Pass B: 'the Logos accomplished each thing in turn' for 'τὸ κατὰ ἓν λόγος ἀπετελεῖτο' adds content ('each thing in turn') not present in the Greek to compensate for a poor translation of 'κατὰ ἓν'.
